department: Biomedical Engineering Graduate Program (Schulich School of Engineering)

deadline.value: International applicants for September 2027 apply by March 1, 2027. Year inferred.
deadline.quote: International (students with international transcripts)- apply by March 1

gre_general.value: The program lists no required test scores, so the GRE is not needed.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: You are admitted only once an approved supervisor agrees to supervise and fund you.
supervisor.quote: Students can only be accepted upon identification of one or more approved Biomedical Graduate Engineering Program supervisors who are willing to supervise and fund the applicant.

funding.value: Every full-time PhD student is guaranteed at least CAD 33,205 a year (international; CAD 31,426 domestic) for the first four years, if progress stays satisfactory.
funding.quote: Full-time PhD students beginning their program on or after January 1, 2026, are guaranteed a minimum funding package of $31,426 for domestic students and $33,205 for international students. | These annual amounts are guaranteed for the first four years of a PhD program

entry_route.value: A four-year bachelor's plus a thesis MSc in engineering, science or kinesiology is required; MSc students may transfer into the PhD.
entry_route.quote: A four-year baccalaureate degree and a Master of Science (thesis) degree or equivalent in engineering, science, kinesiology or equivalent, from a recognized institution.
